key_insight: Multi-agent collaboration is not always better: as language models get more capable, the benefits of teaming up can shrink or even disappear. The paper also shows a predictive model can often choose the best collaboration setup, correctly selecting architectures in 87% of held-out within-domain cases.
problem_solved: This paper addresses when multi-agent language model collaboration actually improves performance versus when it adds unnecessary complexity or reduces results. It helps practitioners decide whether to use single-agent or multi-agent setups for a given task.
method: Ran a controlled study across 260 multi-agent and single-agent configurations of large language model systems.
Compared performance to identify patterns where collaboration helps, hurts, or offers no advantage.
Built a predictive model to recommend the best architecture for a given task/configuration.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work provides evidence that collaboration should be chosen strategically, not assumed to be beneficial. It can save compute and engineering effort by helping teams select the simplest effective architecture.
visual_elements: Decision tree or flowchart showing when to use single-agent vs multi-agent setups
Performance comparison bar chart across the 260 configurations
Scatter plot illustrating model capability vs collaboration benefit
Architecture diagram of the predictive selector choosing the best setup
paper_title: Capable language models can outgrow the benefits of collaboration
paper_authors: Yubin Kim, Ken Gu, Chanwoo Park, Chunjong Park, Samuel Schmidgall
